findings.issue: No error.tsx or global-error.tsx anywhere; the app is 100% dynamic-rendered against a live API, so a single 5xx throws out of a server component and the user gets Next's default unstyled error page.
findings.suggestion: Add a route-level error.tsx (and a global-error.tsx for the root) rendering the standard layout with a 'Something went wrong' heading and a retry link.

findings.issue: spriteUrl() hardcodes /media/sprites/pokemon/.png and every card renders an , ignoring sprites.front_default which the API sets to null for unshipped sprites — a species without a front sprite shows a broken image.
findings.suggestion: Pass the sprite URL (or null) through CardData and render the img conditionally, keeping the hardcoded pattern only as a fallback.

findings.issue: decodeURIComponent is applied to params Next has already decoded (same in moves/abilities/types pages), so a Pokémon name containing a literal % sequence would be double-decoded and 404.
findings.suggestion: Rely on Next's decoding; key(name) already lowercases and encodes for the API path.

findings.issue: Default-variety→Pokémon resolution is duplicated between the Pokémon page's loadSpecies and the team page's loadMembers; the next consumer will copy it again.
findings.suggestion: Add a getDefaultPokemon(species) helper in lib/api.ts and use it from both call sites.

findings.issue: Home page fetches getSpeciesIndex() plus getAllTypes()/getGenerations() separately; they only dedupe because of the module TTL cache, so a cold cache briefly triples the request set and a future change could desync them.
findings.suggestion: Wrap getAllTypes/getGenerations in React cache() (as pages already do for resource loads) or have getSpeciesIndex return the labels it already computed.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled TTL/LRU cache with a concurrency queue reimplements what Next 16's cacheComponents/use cache + cacheLife provide, and the queue is a subtle piece of infra a maintainer must reason about (e.g. cache.set ordering, tee-drain comment at api.ts:47).
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is given cacheComponents is opt-in, but document the choice at the top of api.ts or migrate to 'use cache' with cacheLife when the team enables cacheComponents.

summary: A genuinely idiomatic current-generation Next.js App Router app: correct use of async params, connection(), cached metadata, server-only boundaries and a clean colocated-component layout, with unusually good why-comments. The merge blockers are small: no error boundary despite fully live data loading, and a hardcoded sprite URL that ignores the API's null sprites. I'd approve after one short round addressing those and two minor duplications.
